descriptionChirho: Aramaic verb (Pe'al) meaning to hear or listen, used of auditory perception and attentive reception of speech. In Dan 3:5, 7, 15 it describes hearing the sound of musical instruments as the signal to worship the golden image; in Dan 5:14, 16 Daniel's reputation for hearing and understanding is referenced by the queen and king; in Dan 6:14 the king heard the accusation against Daniel; in Dan 5:23 the gods of the Babylonians cannot hear. All multilingual glosses converge on 'hear/hoeren/entendre/escuchar' with Hindi 'sunna' and Korean 'deutda.'

Aramaic Hitpael reflexive-intensive form meaning to obey, show obedience, or submit to authority -- a semantic extension of hearing into compliance and submission. Used in Dan 7:27 where all dominions shall serve and obey the saints of the Most High. The Hitpael stem marks the intensified, reflexive sense of 'making oneself hear' = obeying. Spanish 'obedeceraan,' Hindi 'aagyaa maanenge' (obey a command), Korean 'sunjonghal geosida' (will submit) all confirm the distinct 'obey' rather than mere 'hear' semantics.
